key_insight: The paper introduces a way to keep long-term memory for dynamic novel view synthesis without paying the full cost of gradient updates at every frame. This makes online, real-time reconstruction of streaming multi-view video more practical.
problem_solved: It addresses the trade-off between persistent memory for occluded or changing scene regions and the strict latency requirements of real-time online novel view synthesis from multi-view streaming videos.
method: Uses an online neural space-time memory mechanism to retain information across long video horizons.
Reduces dependence on heavy test-time training updates at every frame, improving efficiency for dynamic scenes.
Balances memory persistence and adaptation so the model can handle motion and temporary occlusions in streaming settings.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more deployable path to real-time 3D scene reconstruction and view synthesis from video streams. It is especially relevant for robotics, AR/VR, telepresence, and any application that needs fast adaptation without expensive per-frame optimization.

paper_title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Baback Elmieh, Lynn Tsai, Zeman Li, Srinivas Kaza, Tiancheng Sun
